title: Silas (Silvanus)
lead: Silas, called Silvanus in the letters, was a leader and prophet of the Jerusalem church who became Paul's partner on his second journey through Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea and Corinth. He is named as co-sender of 1 and 2 Thessalonians, and a Silvanus carried or wrote 1 Peter.

sections.b: Silas is one of the two "men who led among the brothers" (Acts 15:22) chosen to carry the Jerusalem council's letter to Antioch (Acts 15:27), and a prophet (Acts 15:32), and Paul chose him for his second journey (Acts 15:40). He was beaten and jailed with Paul at Philippi (Acts 16:19-40), helped found the churches of Thessalonica and Berea (Acts 17:1-14), and rejoined Paul in Corinth with Timothy (Acts 18:5).

Paul names him Silvanus, the fuller Latin-looking form, as a preacher at Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:19) and as co-sender of both letters to Thessalonica (1 Thessalonians 1:1; 2 Thessalonians 1:1). 1 Peter 5:12 says the letter came through Silvanus, which may mean he carried it or helped write it.
